newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil flat, apart from correcting barges.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil flat, apart from correcting barges.

text.p: Fuel oil in northern Europe was steady to flat on Friday with little physical trade done.
High sulphur barges recovered Thursday's losses, trading up to $125 fob ARA. "It was a correction to yesterday, which was seen oversold," said one barge trader.

High sulphur cargoes were flat around $115-117 fob NWE and likely to remain so next week. NWE utilities, understood to be discreetly looking for material, have not so far followed an Irish power company's lead of buying Russian straight-run.
"At least two end-users could accommodate the water content, but they have not being tempted yet," said one trader.
The easy availability of Russian straight-run, which in some cases has been sold below the cracked price, was not expected to depress cracked prices significantly.
"There's a feeling the market is here to stay with supply getting tighter as we go into winter," said one broker.
Low sulphur cracked cargoes were steady around $124-126 fob NWE, still showing a slight discount to October paper. Business was quiet
